q: What is the chromatic number χ(G) of a graph?
options: The fewest colours needed so that adjacent vertices differ
explain: For example, a triangle needs 3 colours, and any bipartite graph with at least one edge needs exactly 2.

q: What is χ of a cycle with 7 vertices?
explain: Odd cycles are not bipartite, so 2 colours fail. Alternating two colours and using a third for the last vertex works.

q: What is χ of the complete graph Kₙ?
explain: Every pair of vertices is adjacent, so all n colours must be different.

q: In m-colouring backtracking, when may vertex v receive colour c?
options: When no already-coloured neighbour of v has colour c
When c is the smallest colour
When v has degree less than c
explain: This is the bounding function. Uncoloured neighbours are checked later, when their turn comes.

q: In the Sudoku-as-a-graph view, what are the vertices and edges?
options: Cells; edges join cells in the same row, column or box
explain: A valid Sudoku is then a proper colouring with 9 colours that agrees with the given clues.

q: Deciding whether a graph can be coloured with 2 colours is NP-complete.
explain: False. 2-colourability is the same as being bipartite, which BFS checks in O(V + E). It is 3-colourability that is NP-complete.

q: What is the worst-case number of colour assignments tried by m-colouring backtracking on n vertices?
explain: Each of the n vertices can take m colours, so the tree has up to mⁿ leaves.

q: In a 9 × 9 Sudoku, for cell (r, c) with 0-based indices, where does its 3 × 3 box start?
options: Row r − r mod 3, column c − c mod 3
Row r mod 3, column c mod 3
explain: For example, cell (5, 7) is in the box that starts at (3, 6).

q: Colouring vertices in a fixed order with the smallest free colour (greedy) always uses χ(G) colours.
explain: False. A bad vertex order can make greedy use many more colours than needed, even on bipartite graphs.

q: Exam timetabling: subjects are vertices and an edge joins two subjects that share a student. What does a colour stand for?
explain: Subjects with an edge between them must be in different slots. The chromatic number is the fewest slots needed.
